case.question: Propose a launch menu for both Dubai and Abu Dhabi, with portions and localization.
expected: Meaty pizza and kebab sandwich identity retained
Portions and adaptations explained as proposals

answer.headline: A shared core launch menu built around meaty pizza and kebab sandwiches, with a small city-specific localization layer; portion and price points must be set after your own recipe costing since your concept is not the same as the competitors observed.

sections.title: Menu architecture: shared national core, thin local layer

items.text: Launch one national core menu across Dubai and Abu Dhabi so prep, training and supplier specs stay identical, then add only a few city-specific items. Observed multi-branch operators publish one shared UAE menu rather than different menus per emirate, which suggests a shared-core approach is workable in this market without proving it is right for your concept.

Proposed national core (groups only, no prices yet): 4-5 meaty pizzas; 4-5 kebab/shawarma sandwiches; 1-2 wraps; 1 large-format sharing pizza; 2 sides; 1-2 desserts; 2 drinks. Keep the launch list short enough that one kitchen line can execute it consistently at peak.

Competitor menus observed in both cities include pizza alongside Levantine sandwich and manakish categories, and shawarma sandwiches in Abu Dhabi. So sandwiches and pizza are commonly offered side by side in this segment, but this does not tell you what your specific audience will buy or how to differentiate; treat it as format context only.

sections.title: Portions and sizing: use published size tiers as format precedent, then cost your own

items.text: Observed competitor pizza sizing precedent: an 8-inch tier, a 10-inch tier and a 13-inch tier, with the 8-inch also used as a single-person meal bundle component. Observed sandwich sizing precedent in Abu Dhabi: small, regular and large labels on the same shawarma sandwich. Neither source states gram weights or pizza diameter for every item, so these are label and inch precedents only.

Proposed portion plan for launch testing: pizza in three sizes (single, personal/regular, sharing); kebab sandwiches in regular and large only, plus a wrapped 'saj'-style variant because a saj bread variant is already sold in this segment; sides in single and sharing sizes. Test actual gram weights in-store and lock them into a spec sheet rather than copying competitor labels, which were not specified.

All launch prices should be set from your own recipe costing, packaging cost and channel commission, not from the competitor prices below. The observed prices are individual menu items in anonymous delivery listings with no branch checkout, so they exclude delivery charges, extras and verified tax treatment and cannot be treated as your achievable price or as a city average.

sections.title: Localization: differences worth testing, not assumed preferences

items.text: The evidence does not establish what customers in Dubai or Abu Dhabi prefer, and no source shows a Dubai-versus-Abu-Dhabi menu difference for these operators. Any city-level localization below is a proposition to test, not a finding.

Dubai localization to test: a late-night sandwich and pizza combo, since a competitor in Dubai advertises delivery until 4 AM; and a tourist-corridor-friendly single-person pizza bundle. Advertised competitor hours do not establish overnight demand in your catchment, so validate with a limited-hours trial before committing.

Abu Dhabi localization to test: an office/ADNOC-adjacent lunch sandwich and manakish-adjacent flatbread line, given observed Khalifa City sandwich and manakish listings and an early 8 AM advertised opening at a Khalifa City competitor. Competitor presence and hours do not establish demand at your site; treat this as a testable hypothesis with measured sell-through.

Halal, Arabic-first naming and clear allergen labelling are proposals for both cities that require verification with the relevant UAE authorities and your suppliers; the retrieved sources do not cover licensing, halal certification or allergen rules.

sections.title: Cross-check: observed competitor price points for context only

items.text: Dubai, a Levantine fast-food operator in JBR: pepperoni pizza AED 40 and margherita AED 38; falafel sandwich regular AED 13, large AED 18, saj AED 19; vegetarian halloumi wrap AED 35. These are single-branch delivery-listing items with no diameter or weight given.

UAE-wide pizza chain web menu: All The Meats and Butter Chicken pizzas each AED 33 (8 inch), AED 50 (10 inch), AED 69 (13 inch); a solo meal of one 8-inch pizza, wedges and a canned drink at AED 37. Abu Dhabi Khalifa City: chicken shawarma small AED 11, regular AED 15.50, large AED 26; zaatar manakish AED 12, Akkawi and lahm b ajine manakish AED 22 each.

Read these as tier anchors only: they show that size-tiered pizza and size-tiered sandwiches are already sold in both cities, but they are single items in unaudited listings and cannot be treated as a market price band or a target margin.

assumptions: Concept constraint from your profile: Jordanian restaurant specializing in meaty pizza and kebab sandwiches (user input, not researched).
Target cities Dubai and Abu Dhabi (user input).

I did not have your recipe costs, target food-cost percentage, portion weights, packaging costs, delivery commission, rent or fixed costs, so no price, contribution or break-even figure is proposed here.
Any Dubai late-night or Abu Dhabi lunch/office localization is a hypothesis to test; the evidence does not establish demand, footfall or preferences.
next_steps: Write one spec sheet per launch item: portion weight, dough ball weight, number of skewers, bread type and side inclusion. Weigh finished portions in-store for a week and lock tolerances.
Cost each item from your own invoices for meat, cheese, bread and packaging in both cities; convert to a target price only after food cost and channel commission are known.
Run a two-week limited trial of the Dubai late-night sandwich/pizza bundle and the Abu Dhabi lunch flatbread/sandwich set, and record sell-through per item before expanding the menu.
Set prices separately for dine-in/takeaway and each delivery channel, since observed competitor listings are unaudited item prices and do not show fees or taxes.

If you want a priced menu and a margin check, supply these eight values so I can run unit economics: average order revenue, food cost per order, packaging per order, other variable cost per order, delivery share, delivery commission rate, monthly fixed costs, and operating days per month.
